title: Why Does Your Phone Go Dark Through Sunglasses? #science
description:
Your screen never switched off: your polarized sunglasses blocked it. Many phone screens send out light that wiggles one way only (polarized light). Polarized sunglasses are a filter too: worn upright they pass up-and-down wiggles, to block glare off roads and water. Lined up, the light gets through; turned a quarter turn, the filters cross and almost nothing passes (Malus's law, I = I₀ cos²θ). Tilt your head and the picture usually comes back.

Caveat: many phones set their polarization at 45° or add a film so the screen stays visible either way; then it only dims. Which orientation goes dark depends on the model.

More on waves cancelling: How do headphones cancel noise with more noise? https://youtu.be/rOxQ3PFvewk

Sources
- OpenStax, University Physics Volume 3, 1.7 Polarization (Malus's law, polarization by reflection, LCDs)
- Hecht, E., Optics (5th ed., 2017), chapter 8 Polarization

subtitles: Why does your phone go dark through sunglasses?
Tilt your head, and the picture usually comes back.
Light is a wave, and it can wiggle in any direction.
Many phone screens only let out light that wiggles one way.
Polarized sunglasses are a filter too.
Worn upright, they only pass up-and-down wiggles, to block the glare off roads and water.
Line the two filters up, and the light gets through.
Turn one a quarter turn, and they cross.
